simt.name: SIMT
simt.definition: Single Instruction, Multiple Threads: one instruction issued to a warp, each thread working on its own data.

warp.name: Warp
warp.definition: 32 threads that the hardware issues together and runs in lockstep.

lane.name: Lane
lane.definition: One of the 32 positions in a warp; thread t of a block is lane t mod 32.

sm.name: SM
sm.definition: Streaming multiprocessor: one of the GPU's compute tiles, with its own schedulers, registers and shared memory.

gigathread.name: GigaThread Engine
gigathread.definition: The chip-level scheduler that hands thread blocks to SMs.

gpc.name: GPC
gpc.definition: Graphics processing cluster: a group of SMs that share some front-end hardware.

block.name: Thread block
block.definition: A group of threads that run on one SM, can synchronize and can share memory.

grid.name: Grid
grid.definition: All the blocks of one kernel launch.

occupancy.name: Occupancy
occupancy.definition: Resident warps on an SM divided by the maximum the SM can hold.

coalescing.name: Coalescing
coalescing.definition: Combining a warp's memory accesses into as few memory transactions as possible.

sector.name: Sector
sector.definition: The 32-byte unit in which the memory system fetches data.

bank.name: Bank
bank.definition: One of the 32 independent slices of shared memory; a bank serves one 4-byte word per cycle.

bank-conflict.name: Bank conflict
bank-conflict.definition: Two or more lanes of a warp asking the same bank for different words, so the access is serialized.

divergence.name: Divergence
divergence.definition: Lanes of one warp taking different branches; the warp runs each path in turn with the other lanes masked.

reconvergence.name: Reconvergence
reconvergence.definition: The point where diverged lanes of a warp rejoin and run together again.

predication.name: Predication
predication.definition: Executing both sides of a short condition and keeping only the right result, instead of branching.

roofline.name: Roofline
roofline.definition: A plot of attainable FLOP/s against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak compute and by memory bandwidth.

arithmetic-intensity.name: Arithmetic intensity
arithmetic-intensity.definition: FLOPs performed per byte moved to and from memory.

ridge-point.name: Ridge point
ridge-point.definition: The arithmetic intensity at which peak compute equals what memory bandwidth can feed.

pcie.name: PCIe
pcie.definition: The bus between the host CPU and the GPU; much slower than the GPU's own memory.

hbm.name: HBM
hbm.definition: High-bandwidth memory stacked next to the GPU die (A100, H100).

l2.name: L2 cache
l2.definition: The chip-wide cache between the SMs and DRAM.

shared-memory.name: Shared memory
shared-memory.definition: Fast on-chip memory, per block, managed by the programmer.

register-spill.name: Register spill
register-spill.definition: A value that did not fit in registers and lives in slow local memory instead.

atomic.name: Atomic
atomic.definition: A read-modify-write that no other thread can interleave with.

fence.name: Memory fence
fence.definition: An instruction that orders a thread's own memory writes as seen by other threads.

shuffle.name: Shuffle
shuffle.definition: A warp instruction that moves a register value from one lane to another.

nccl.name: NCCL
nccl.definition: NVIDIA's library of multi-GPU collectives such as AllReduce.

allreduce.name: AllReduce
allreduce.definition: A collective that sums (or otherwise combines) a tensor across GPUs and gives every GPU the result.

nvlink.name: NVLink
nvlink.definition: A direct GPU-to-GPU link that is much faster than PCIe.

wave.name: Wave
wave.definition: One round of blocks filling all the SMs; a grid of many blocks runs in several waves.

ilp.name: ILP
ilp.definition: Instruction-level parallelism: independent instructions within one thread that can be in flight together.

stream.name: Stream
stream.definition: An ordered queue of GPU work; work in different streams may overlap.

halo.name: Halo
halo.definition: The border cells a tile needs from its neighbour in a stencil or a split grid.

eta.name: eta (efficiency)
eta.definition: The fraction of a peak that a real kernel achieves; used in time predictions.

alpha-beta.name: alpha-beta model
alpha-beta.definition: Time to send n bytes = latency alpha + n / bandwidth beta.

swizzle.name: Swizzle
swizzle.definition: Permuting where data is stored (for example with XOR) to avoid bank conflicts.

csr.name: CSR
csr.definition: Compressed sparse row: a sparse matrix stored as values, column indices and row pointers.

ulp.name: Unit roundoff
ulp.definition: The largest relative rounding error of one operation in a number format.

mixed-precision.name: Mixed precision
mixed-precision.definition: Storing and multiplying in a narrow format while accumulating in a wider one.

cuda-graph.name: CUDA graph
cuda-graph.definition: A recorded sequence of GPU work launched with a single call.
